anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer persistently chooses a substantially sub-optimal execution plan even though statistics are accurate.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes saturate host CPU, leaving too few cycles for the rest of the workload.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : Client-server transport or connection-handling infrastructure becomes a throughput bottleneck, causing delays in establishing or servicing sessions.

Composite definition: The database simultaneously suffers from sub-optimal plan selection, host-level CPU saturation, and constrained network/connection capacity. Together these three root causes create a multilayer performance crisis in which inefficient plans generate excessive CPU demand while the network layer cannot move data or establish sessions fast enough, amplifying latency and error rates across the entire workload.

Combined observable phenomena: 1) Drastic and frequent plan flips that favor full scans or over-parallelized execution, driving CPU usage to sustained 90-100 %. 2) Run-queue depth, context switches, and CPU-bound wait events coincide with surges in client-side connect or read timeouts, "too many connections" errors, and growing server backlog queues. 3) Statement latency and throughput become highly variable; some sessions wait on CPU, others stall on client-read/client-write waits, and retry storms escalate both CPU and network pressure. 4) Monitoring shows a mismatch between cached plan costs and actual resource consumption, steep spikes in network retransmissions, and a sudden plateau in completed transactions per second despite rising workload demand.

Causal interaction: Sub-optimal plans inflate row processing, parallelism, and result-set size, directly raising CPU cycles consumed per statement and volume of bytes sent over the wire. The surge in CPU contention slows process scheduling, lengthening every network handshake, authentication, and data send, which in turn keeps back-end sessions open longer and exhausts listener sockets. Connection stalls and retries feed an even higher request rate into the server, causing the optimizer to compile more ad-hoc statements and cache additional poor plans, closing the feedback loop. The intertwined effects of inefficient planning, CPU starvation, and network congestion therefore reinforce one another, driving the system into a self-amplifying saturation state that is harder to diagnose because symptoms span optimizer, operating-system, and network layers simultaneously.

entry.official_definition: Aborts any statement that takes more than the specified amount of time; zero disables the timeout.
entry.trigger_condition: A SQL statement runs longer than statement_timeout, measured from command arrival until completion.
entry.workload_impact: The running statement is aborted; when configured, the timed-out statement is logged.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
